snippet.textDisplay: I’m 59 and just lost my dad who was 82.  In the last years leading g up to his passing, tge caregiving slowly ratcheted up until it’s like I had a second full-time job. snippet.textDisplay: My 91 yr. Old dad passed at his home (palliative care) in 2020 from cancer. My sister, brother in-law and I took turns sleeping there every night and all days weekends to tend to him. Mom was too old. We had to pay "angels" during the day while at work. My mom passed in 2024 at 88 after a TBI and stroke. We had yp pay for 24 hrs. Care for her even when she was in rehab and then at home because the USA and well known insurance gave us minimal help. We used their retirement money luckily but It was exhausting. I look back and wouldn't have wanted it any other way. You will get through this. You are strong. I hope you have others to help. No one cares for the caregiver. If it gets too much and they need to be placed somewhere, that is ok too. No guilt. It's overwhelming. Hugs.

snippet.textDisplay: Yes, I just finished that journey with my Mum last November. It was all consuming, and so much more difficult than parenting. It was logistically difficult, though my sisters snd I teamed up to share in her care. Admin was nightmarish, finding the programs she was eligible for, and then actually getting her into them. And especially emotionally to parent your parent, and grieve the loss of them before they’ve even transitioned on. But all consuming as it was, I am so grateful we did it, and that my sister and I each had the privilege of holding her hand, and walking her home the day after Thanksgiving last year. I know it’s hard, so fucking hard, but it’s worth it, and I’m wildly cheering you on!

snippet.textDisplay: Dad passed away, due to dementia. Mom took care of him (with my assistance).  They lived 3 hrs away from me.  I researched homes for Dad to go to.  We did the shifting of bank accounts to be in mom's name.  He knew he needed to get rid of anything in his name, so there'd be less stress on mom.  Mom lives alone now.  She seems great.  She has a Jeopardy Caledar which asks her questions daily.  She texts the question to me every morning.  I reply and she keeps track of our scores.  This has been a great way to keep tabs on her.  There is nobody else left from her family.  I'm her only child and her parents/sisters/friends have all passed.  Thankfully, she has good neighbours.  I feel for you.  It is tough to be consumed by it.  Total stress.  If your loved one goes into the hospital and is way too hard for you to deal with (like mobility issues/nursing care/fights/etc.) say these words: "He/She/They cannot come home"  'NO!"  Because, if you say you'll pick them up, or indicate that they can come home, you are now TOTALLY responsible for them.  Whereas, in hospital, they are TOTALLY responsible for them.  Do what is best for you and your family, as well as what is best for elderly.

snippet.textDisplay:
I am an elderly sinle parent being cared for in my home. My brother convinced my daughter to live with me she has her own family.
I do NOT have dementia confirmed by doctors. I hurt to see her here day by day crying for me. I am not helpless. I want to exit my home but I don’t want to go to a caged facility. I’ve made several offers to make other arrangements

I don’t want her to feel she has to be here because she doesn’t have to be.

I can feel the tension. I’ve had several falls which I call the rescue squad.

What does a parent do in this situation. My heart goes out to you midlife with young adults or kids.

You shouldn’t be struggling with your mom. Seek out help from county/state help.

May God bless and keep you all the parental caretakers.
